title: Derived categories of module sheaves have direct sums
statement: For every scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and every set-indexed family $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ in the derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, the termwise direct sum of any representative complexes represents a direct sum of the $E_i$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. For every integer $q$, its cohomology sheaf is canonically isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i\in I} H^q(E_i)$.

source.place: Lemma 07D9 (lemma-derived-products), clauses (1)-(2); the cohomology identity is in perfect.tex, proof of Lemma 08DT (lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-sums), from exactness of direct sums

proof.text: By [lem-pc-scheme-modules-grothendieck-abelian], the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is Grothendieck abelian. Therefore it has the required set-indexed coproducts and these coproducts are exact.

Choose representative complexes $E_i^\bullet$ for the objects $E_i$. In the category of complexes, coproducts are computed degreewise, so the complex $E^\bullet=\bigoplus_iE_i^\bullet$ has the termwise direct-sum coprojections. Exact coproducts preserve quasi-isomorphisms and the localization defining the derived category, so the image of $E^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ satisfies the coproduct universal property. This remains valid for the empty and singleton families.

For each degree $q$, exactness of set-indexed direct sums in the abelian category of sheaves of modules gives $H^q(\bigoplus_iE_i^\bullet)\cong\bigoplus_iH^q(E_i^\bullet)$: kernels and images of the termwise differential commute with the direct sum, and the quotient of cycles by boundaries is therefore the direct sum of the corresponding quotients. The isomorphism is canonical and is induced by the coprojection maps.
